messages:
maria: heads up — prod started OOMing on longctx endpoints right after the 1.17.1 rollout, multiple nodes hit OOM within 20m. stack trace shows slab alloc growth in kv_cache. @ops-jen can you take a look? :alarm_clock:
perf-bot: [CI] nightly/memory regression detected: +2.8GB median resident memory vs baseline (job: runtime-memory-nightly).
deploy-bot: rollout v1.17.1 finished at 2026-03-18T09:12:30Z (canaries passed).
todd: any recent kernel-selection or batching heuristic changes in that release?
jelani: I started a bisect on the release range. initial result points to commit abc1234ef (kernel routing heuristics) — changes how we prioritize low-latency kernels for mixed sequence workloads.
asha: copying profiler snapshot from canary that OOM'd — seems kv_cache slab for seqlen>1024 jumped a lot:
```
heap-summary:
  total: 12.4GB -> 15.6GB
  kv_cache_slab_longseq: 1.2GB -> 4.1GB
  slab_frag_percent: 14% -> 29%
  top-alloc-sites:
    - kv_cache::reserve_prefix
    - slab::grow
```
jelani: bisect commands I ran:
```
git bisect start v1.17.1 v1.16.9
git bisect bad abc1234ef
git bisect good 9f8b7c6d
# result: abc1234ef is first bad commit
```
jelani: that commit altered kernel_selection::score() to favor kernels with lower overhead for small batches, but the fallback logic accidentally prevents switching to low-memory kernels when sequence_length distribution skews long. So long sequences keep being routed to a high-throughput kernel that retains large KV pages.
todd: so kernel choice change indirectly increased per-request kv retention. can we force the kernel selector to include seqlen-weighted memory cost?
asha: quick patch I tried locally — add a seqlen_bias into score: score -= (seqlen/1024) * mem_penalty. perf run on local rig shows resident drop ~1.8GB for longctx workload.
jelani: filing PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4567 — fixes selector and adds an integration test that simulates skewed seqlen distribution.
ops-jen: mitigation for prod: change runtime config to tighten kv eviction for >1024 tokens (evict_window_ms -> 50ms) and pin kernel to legacy-lowmem for the canary pool. rolling that now to canary group.
perf-bot: ran quick perf job against canary with pinned kernel + eviction tweak: memory stable, no OOM within 30m, tokens/sec -2% (expected tradeoff).
maria: thanks. todd please coordinate rollback of full rollout until PR merged + canary observed for 1h. open rollback ticket?
todd: on it — opening ticket ROLLBACK-789 and starting rollback of v1.17.1 full rollout.
deploy-bot: rollback of v1.17.1 initiated at 2026-03-18T10:05:12Z.
asha: note — this also explains CI perf regression: nightly uses long-seq test bedding, which tipped memory above CI threshold.
jelani: after patch + config tweak I re-ran stress with 3h longctx mixed workload: no OOMs, slab frag stabilized at ~16%.
ops-jen: canary nodes healthy, no OOMs for 45m. Marking incident mitigated for now.
maria: please add a short postmortem blurb (root cause: kernel selector heuristic change caused long-seq routing to high-memory kernel -> kv slab growth) and cite PR/4567 and ROLLBACK-789. we'll follow up with a longer postmortem. :white_check_mark:
perf-bot: CI regression guard updated to include seqlen-skewed memory test (PR 4570).
jelani: will land PR after a couple of LGs and ramp config in prod slowly. thanks all for quick triage.
